about.title: Shasta Lake Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Shasta Lake is a small city along the shores of Lake Shasta, and most residents drive Rt 151, Shasta Dam Boulevard, Cascade Boulevard, or Wonderland Boulevard to get around Shasta County. But defective products don't just cause problems on the road — a faulty vehicle part, a malfunctioning tool, a contaminated consumer good, or unsafe machinery at a job site can injure someone at home, at work, or in transit through town. California's strict liability rules for defective products mean an injured person generally doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent, only that the product itself was flawed and that the flaw caused harm. If a defective product has hurt you or someone in your family here in Shasta Lake, our team can evaluate your case at no cost. We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters Under California Law

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California generally allows injured people to hold manufacturers responsible by showing a product was defective, without having to prove negligence. This can make pursuing a claim more straightforward than other injury cases.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable for a defective product under California law. Our team can help identify every party connected to the product that caused your injury.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Keeping the defective product exactly as it was at the time of injury is often critical evidence in these claims. We can advise you early on how to protect and document it properly.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability approach to defective products, you generally need to show the product had a defect — in its design, manufacturing, or warnings — and that this defect caused your injury. This is different from many other injury claims where negligence must be proven.

items.question: What if the injury happened somewhere other than a road in Shasta Lake?
items.answer: That's fine — product liability claims can arise anywhere a defective item is used, whether at home, at work, or while traveling on corridors like Shasta Dam Boulevard or Cascade Boulevard. What matters is the product itself and how it caused harm, not the location.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury occurred, and avoid throwing it away or attempting repairs. The product often serves as key evidence, and our team can advise you on preserving it properly.
